q: The faces in my interview look grey and sickly but the rest is fine.
a: 1. Balance the whole shot first. 2. Add a node for skin (`grade.addNode`, name it Skin with `grade.labelNode`). 3. Qualifier: Pick on a cheek (`grade.pickQualifier`), Add a lighter and a darker patch, check View ▸ Matte. 4. In Primaries, a small push of Gain towards orange and a little Saturation inside the matte. Small is the point: too orange is worse than grey. Check skin against the vectorscope's skin line.

q: skin fix also turned the wooden table orange
a: Wood shares skin's hue: narrow Hue width and raise Saturation low a little, or add a soft window around the faces on the same node (`masks.add`, tracked with `masks.track`) so the node acts only where both select.

q: Grey skin after normalising F-Log2, on 40 interview clips.
a: Fix one clip with the skin node, then copy that node to the others (`grade.append`) and check each: skin keys can need small hue-width changes per clip. Check scene (`grade.checkScene`) finds clips that drift.

q: The scene starts happy and turns sad; I want the colour to cool down with it.
a: Keyframe a grade across the turn: Lumetri on the clip (`effects.apply`, `lumetri`) with Temperature, Saturation and Exposure keyframed from warm and bright to cool and muted over the moment of change, eased (`effects.setInterpolation`). For a change across several shots, put Lumetri on an Adjustment Layer above them so one set of keyframes covers all.

q: colour drains out slowly as the character gets lonelier through the film
a: Grade per section rather than one keyframe: copy the look node with a little less saturation to each later scene (`grade.append` then adjust), so the progression is gradual and controllable. Lumetri keyframes on an Adjustment Layer work inside a scene.

q: Sudden switch from colour to cold blue when the twist hits.
a: Cut the clip at the twist (`sequence.addEdit`) and give the second piece its own cool grade; a Dip to White or a hard cut on a sound hit sells the switch.

q: Zoom into a TV in the shot until its picture fills the frame and becomes the next scene.
a: 1. Put the next scene on V2 pinned onto the TV with Corner Pin and Track Surface (`tracking.cornerPin`). 2. Nest V1 and V2 together (`clip.nest`) and keyframe the nest's Motion Scale and Position up towards the screen, eased. 3. At the point the screen fills the frame, cut to the next scene full-frame (same frame of it) so it continues sharp.

q: zoom into the phone screen in my hand and go into the app recording
a: Same idea: the screen recording corner-pinned onto the phone, the pair nested, a Scale push into the screen, then cut to the recording at full size. A short Cross Zoom transition can hide the switch.

q: Pull back out of a monitor to reveal the room.
a: Reverse it: start on the monitor content full frame, cut to the nested room shot already scaled in on the monitor, and keyframe Scale back to 100 %; the content must be corner-pinned on the monitor in the room shot.

q: Reveal my photo with a paintbrush stroke wiping across it.
a: Animate a mask: A Bézier or rectangle mask on the photo's Opacity (`masks.add`), its path keyframed across the frame with a heavy feather; a brush-stroke clip on transparency over it (Screen or Multiply) adds the painted edge.

q: ink spreading reveal from the centre
a: An ellipse mask on Opacity starting tiny in the centre, keyframed larger with high feather (Mask Expansion helps); an ink-blot overlay clip on Multiply for texture.

q: Title revealed by a handwritten stroke.
a: A rectangle mask on the title, its edge keyframed left to right so letters appear as if drawn; for real handwriting, many small mask keyframes or an animation made elsewhere.

q: A TV channel wants my film; what do I change for broadcast?
a: 1. Loudness: their spec (EBU R128 −23 LUFS or ATSC −24 LKFS), measured with the loudness meter, a limiter on the Mix for the peak ceiling. 2. Levels: the export's video limiter for legal levels (web deliveries don't need it); don't limit twice. 3. Captions as a file if they ask. 4. Their codec / frame rate preset.

q: broadcaster rejected for illegal levels
a: Turn on the video limiter in the export (or the Video Limiter effect on an Adjustment Layer over the sequence), check the waveform, and re-export. Avoid also crushing with a curve: limiting twice dulls whites.

q: Web and broadcast versions from one edit.
a: Queue two exports: the web one (full range, −14 LUFS) and the broadcast one (limiter, −23 LUFS on a separate mix). A duplicate of the sequence for the broadcast mix keeps both.

q: Foreign street signs in my travel video: add translations next to them that stay put.
a: For each sign, a small label graphic (text with a box pinned to it, `graphics.pin`) on V2 placed next to the sign, then Attach to Track on its Motion (`tracking.attach`, Position only) so it moves with the shot. Keep it on screen long enough to read.

q: replace the text on a sign with the English version
a: Pin an English version (a graphic in a matching font and colour) onto the sign with Corner Pin and Track Surface (`tracking.cornerPin`), with a blend mode or grade so it sits in the light.

q: Translation labels for many signs, same style.
a: Make one label, export it as a template with the text editable (`graphics.template.export`), and apply it per sign.

q: My silent B-roll needs footsteps and small sounds so it feels real.
a: Add footsteps and handling sounds from a sound library on an SFX track, lined up with what you see (frame-step to the contacts); type them SFX in Essential Sound; a quiet ambience bed under all. Keep them a little lower than real so they don't distract.

q: foley sounds too clean compared to the scene
a: Give them the room: a little Reverb (Essential Sound ▸ Creative), an EQ to match the scene's tone, and the same ambience underneath.

q: Line up a punch sound exactly on the impact frame.
a: Step frame by frame to the impact, set a marker (`markers.add`), and snap the sound's start (or its peak) to it with Snap on (`sequence.snap`).

q: Tension scene: the edges of the frame pulse dark with a heartbeat sound.
a: A vignette on an Adjustment Layer: Lumetri's Vignette Amount keyframed in a heartbeat rhythm (two quick pulses, a pause), eased, with a heartbeat sound on an SFX track lined up. Or the Pulse shader recipe at the heart rate for a steady beat.

q: heartbeat gets faster as the danger gets closer
a: Keyframe the pulses closer together towards the climax (or use several pieces with increasing Pulse speed); the heartbeat sound speeds up too: shorter gaps between hits, or a faster loop.

q: Muffled sound plus heartbeat during the shock moment.
a: Cut the highs of the scene's audio with an EQ (keyframed in for the moment), lower it, and bring up the heartbeat; release it all when the shock ends.

q: We shot a scene over three hours and the light changes between shots.
a: Grade the best-lit shot first, then match the others to it (a still and a wipe, or Shot Match), and run Check scene (`grade.checkScene`) to find the drifting ones. Don't make the late shots fully neutral: a little warmth progression reads naturally.

q: clouds came and went, some shots are much darker
a: Match exposure first (Offset / Gain against the reference on the waveform), then contrast, then colour; a tracked window can lift a face that lost its sun.

q: Shadows point different ways between shots.
a: Grading can't move shadows: soften their contrast a little and rely on cutting choices; plan the order of shooting next time.

q: A bright red bin in the background keeps pulling my eye.
a: On its own node, select it (qualifier on the red plus a window around it, tracked if the camera moves) and lower its saturation and brightness until it sinks back. A soft window keeps the edge invisible.

q: bright window behind the interviewee is distracting
a: A window (shape) over it on its own node with Gain down and a soft edge, or a curve shoulder for all highlights; clipped areas stay white, so dim, don't fight it.

q: Logo on a T-shirt I can't show.
a: Blur or Mosaic it with a tracked mask (`tracking.blurRegion` does effect, mask and track in one go); check the track and fix lost frames by hand.
